items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: And much to my surprise upon it was Eddie Miller that had recorded that.

ctx.x: What was the Miller record? Do you remember? It might sometime, Dick.

There was one low register clarinet thing that's become almost a standard, sort of like Bix's chorus on Birth and the Blues, one of these things that's a set of pattern. And much to my surprise upon it was Eddie Miller that had recorded that. It's in one of the standard big band, Dixieland numbers, like Muscat Ramble or Rampage Street, some of that, that's lots of numbers. And Miller, once we played that low, Newman clarinet chorus on it. Right in that shallow, move range of the clarinet, and big sonorous tone…
Yeah, and that was kind of out of fashion then, wasn't it?
